brief.headline: California would put AI violation under Medical Board jurisdiction
brief.alt: A card from the AI Fear Report headed: California would put AI violation under Medical Board jurisdiction. controls.name: Bans and limits on uses of AI
controls.definition: Bans or restricts a use of AI by people or organizations outside government: forbids it outright or for a purpose or setting, such as setting rents, giving therapy or denying insurance claims; requires that a person rather than an AI make or review a decision; requires an AI system to be built so it cannot be used a certain way; or makes creating or spreading AI-made content a crime or a civil violation. Rules for the government's own use of AI do not count.

controls.name: Labels and notices of AI use
controls.definition: Requires labels, watermarks, provenance data, or disclosures on AI-generated content or AI interactions, or requires a company, employer, insurer, landlord, or other private party to tell the people it uses AI on that it is using it.

controls.name: Moratoriums and limits on data centers
controls.definition: Pauses, bans, or adds new permitting restrictions or special conditions on building or operating data centers.

controls.name: New powers for government agencies
controls.definition: Creates a new government office or agency for AI or data centers, or gives an existing agency or attorney general new authority over AI, data centers, or the people and companies who build or use AI, to make rules, inspect, license, or enforce. An office that only oversees the government's own use of AI does not count.

controls.name: Mandatory reporting to government
controls.definition: Requires people or companies outside government that develop, deploy, or operate AI systems, or own or operate data centers, to report, disclose, register, or submit plans, incidents, audits, impact assessments, or other information to a government body, or to produce them on government demand. A government body reporting on its own use of AI does not count.

controls.name: ID and age checks for users
controls.definition: Requires identity verification, age verification, or know-your-customer checks for users, customers, or buyers of AI services or compute.

controls.name: Licenses required to build AI
controls.definition: Requires a license, registration, certification, or government permission before developing, training, or deploying an AI system or model.

controls.name: State laws overridden by Washington
controls.definition: A federal measure that overrides, preempts, or blocks state or local AI laws, or conditions federal funding on states not regulating AI.

controls.name: Export controls on models and chips
controls.definition: Restricts exports or foreign access to AI chips, models, compute, or AI technology.

controls.name: Caps on who can train models
controls.definition: Sets compute, cost, or capability thresholds that trigger restrictions or obligations on who may train or release large AI models.

controls.name: Limits on sharing open models
controls.definition: Restricts publishing, sharing, or open-sourcing AI model weights or code.
